teaching: Al-kamal al-awwal (the first perfection) is the equal, deficiency-free state in which every intellect was originated, given knowledge, life, and power in one single identical state.
Ibda' (origination) happened only once, producing the mubda'at (originated beings), whereas later creation by the Tenth Intellect is called takhliq.
The giver (mu'ti) of the first perfection is the Mabda' Ta'ala Himself.

Al-kamal al-thani (the second perfection) is greater than the first; its giver is a quality born from the beings' own essences (dhawat) through their own effort and preparation, even though the ultimate bestower remains the Mabda'.
A believer-child is born in the state of the first perfection and attains the second perfection when he takes the 'ahd sharif (sacred covenant).

The second perfection is also called wujud al-thani (the second existence), by which the originated essences attained 'azaliyyah (eternity) and complete 'ismah (infallibility), safe from istihala (transformation) and fana' (annihilation).
The Quran's 'yaf'aluna ma yu'marun wa la ya'sun' establishes that the angels do what they are commanded and never disobey or sin.
A vast uncountable number of originated forms (suwar ibda'iyyah) delayed responding to the call and fell behind, following the Tenth Intellect ('Ashir) in his takhalluf.
The intellects above the Tenth, from the ninth up to the inbi'ath al-awwal, through whose intercession (shafa'a) the 'Ashir's repentance was accepted, are called the kalimat (words).
The 'Ashir is the spiritual Adam (Adam al-ruhani), so the Quranic verse 'fa-talaqqa Adam min rabbihi kalimatin fa-taba 'alayhi' applies to him.

The 'Ashir was commanded to turn to his followers (muqtadin) and call them to salvation, on the principle 'man kasara 'azman fa-'alayhi jabruh' (whoever breaks a bone must mend it), which became a proverb.
The Quranic 'law kunta fazzan ghaliz al-qalbi lanfaddu min hawlik' shows the Messenger's gentleness, which all these qualities of compassion in calling were born within him.

The 'Ashir confessed his error as leaving the recognition of the merit of the predecessor ('alam al-muba'ith al-awwal), repented, and urged his followers to repent so they would be fortunate and successful.
The Prophet's saying 'Qulu la ilaha illa Allah, tuflihu' (Say there is no god but Allah and you will be successful) parallels the 'Ashir's call to the fallen to repent.

The followers rejected all merit ('la fadla lahum 'alayna wa-la laka'), arguing 'kulluna ibda' al-Mabda'' and 'abda'ana sawa'an sawa'' — denying the merit of the prior intellects, the Mabda', and the 'Ashir.

The followers' error was looking only at the equal state of the first perfection and refusing to acknowledge the progress attained in the second perfection — like a person dismissing another's spiritual rank by recalling his childhood.

When the fallen insisted on their claim of equality, their essences darkened (azlamat dhawatuhum) after being luminous, they became estranged from the darkness and entangled with one another, becoming the First Matter (al-hayula al-ula).

Three successive movements of the fallen essences produced first length (al-tul al-awwal), then first width (al-'ard al-awwal), then first depth (al-'umq al-awwal), until they became one body (jism wahid) intermingled together.

The reversal of the movements was from the wisdom of the 'Ashir, who was the mutawalli (manager) responsible for governing the disobedient group and arranged for them an abode (dar), instruments (alat), and a call to salvation.

The disobedient varied in their inner intentions and fell into three categories: the repentant seekers of forgiveness (nadim mustaghfir), the doubting bewildered (shakk mutahayyir), and the insistent arrogant (musirr mustakbir).
Sayyidna Isma'il ibn Hibatullah al-Makrami (Da'i al-Shumukh) in his book al-Kawakib al-Durriyyah explained that the hayula divided into 70 parts: 15 repentant, 20 doubters, and 35 insistent.

The recurrence of 70 in tasbihat (e.g. reciting 'Ya Karimu ya Rahimu ya 'Azim, ya ghiyath al-mustaghithin' seventy times) corresponds to the 70 sections of the hayula, and the ghiyath al-mustaghithin invoked is the 'Ashir al-Mudabbir.

The repentant group was noble and did not blame the 'Ashir; they praised and glorified him as they descended, ending with 'al-hamdu lillahi rabb al-'alamin' — where the Lord of the worlds refers to the 'Ashir al-Mudabbir — so their return (raj'at) happened quickly.
The Prophet's ummah dividing into 73 sects corresponds to the 70 sections plus three (the most severe insistent, the most severe doubter, and the purest repentant).

The post-fard tasbih (Allahu Akbar, Alhamdulillah, Subhanallah 33 times each, ending with La ilaha illa Allah) symbolizes the namiya, hissiyya, and natiqa faculties with the noble form, or the Imam's nasut tabi'i, nasut dhilli, nasut khass with his sura sharif.

The tasbih of the sunnat al-fajr ('Subhana rabbi al-'azim wa-bi-hamdihi, astaghfirullah al-'azim wa-atubu ilayh') is the very tasbih the repentant seekers of forgiveness (nadimin mustaghfirin) recited as they fell.
The munajat of the istiftah ('ya rabbi zalamtu nafsi fa-ghfir li... la yaghfiru al-dhanb al-'azim illa anta ya 'Aliyyu ya 'Azim') is from Imam Husayn ibn 'Ali.

Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq narrated that the Lord asks the angels what His servants say in their prostration, and upon hearing they confess wronging their souls and seek His forgiveness, He makes the angels witnesses that He has forgiven and pardoned them.
Allah forgives all sins ('Inna Allah yaghfiru al-dhunub jami'an', 'La taqnatu min rahmat Allah') except shirk, which the Quran calls al-zulm al-'azim.

The 'illa anta' that alone forgives the great sin refers to the Imam of the time, ultimately the 'ayn al-akhirah — the Qa'im 'ala dhikrihi al-salam — who holds the jami'iyyat of 400,000 years (seven satr and seven kashf) and is the qasim al-nar wa-l-jannah (divider of Fire and Garden).
Mawlana 'Ali is also called qasim al-nar wa-l-jannah in a partial sense.
At the gate of paradise people will be stopped and questioned about the walayat of 'Ali — a question on which the great Sunni scholars and all Shia agree.
The forms (suwar) of a believer across successive cycles unite and merge with the later forms, so souls progress across cycles toward settlement.

Yunus, sahib al-hut, said 'la ilaha illa anta, subhanaka inni kuntu min al-zalimin' — combining tawhid, tasbih, and istighfar — and 'la ilaha illa anta' appears only once in the Quran, of greater status than all other forms, directed toward the 'ayn al-'azimah.
Yunus did his tasbih for 40 days, and had he not done it he would have remained in the fish until the Day of Resurrection (yawm yub'athun).
The number 40 carries a power of maturity: a person reaches maturity at 40, the Prophet was made a messenger at age 40, and if 40 people gather and pray for someone their prayer is accepted.

'Umar ibn al-Khattab was the 40th person to accept Islam, upon which the Messenger said Islam had gained strength — likened (per Qutb al-Din) to a house declared built once its final part is completed.

From the 'Ashir's (the Mover's) first motion of the hayula were created the awtad al-falak (pegs of the spheres), four non-visible constellations: tali' (ascendant, east), gharib (descendant, west), 'ashir (mid-sky), and rabi' (under the earth).

When the density overflowed, the four awtad and the two poles (qutba al-falak from north and south) pulled it and held it in the middle of the sphere, the falak encompassing it from all sides like the white and shell encompass an egg's yolk.
The atmosphere split and the spheres were arranged into nine, each sphere contained within the one after it like the layers of an onion.
The falak al-muhit (encompassing sphere) surrounds all spheres and moves them every day and night with one total divine motion by the governing power of the mudabbir, from east to west.

There are seven spheres from Zuhal (Saturn) down to the moon, and all stars reside in the eighth sphere, named the falak al-buruj (sphere of constellations) — just as all believers ultimately gather at the Bab al-Abwab.
The falak al-buruj is divided into twelve constellations (buruj), each with 30 houses, totaling 360 degrees.
The spiritual essences (fudala) ascend through all 360 degrees of the zodiac for purification, traversing them in roughly 720 years of going and coming plus 280 years.

The Quran's 'wa lakum fi al-qisasi hayatun ya uli al-albab' means our very life runs within the vast circle of qisas (retribution), spread across many cycles, not merely that retribution occurs within our life.
The ninth sphere (falak al-muhit) is empty of constellations and planets due to its subtlety and nobility — just as no form gathers with the 'Aql al-Awwal / Mubda' al-Awwal in the spiritual realm.

Two du'at gave two counts of the intellects collected at the Mubda' al-Awwal: Sayyidna 'Ali bin Sulayman said 28 (seeing the 'uqul in totality), Sayyidna Hasan bin Nuh said 12 (the letters of 'La ilaha illa Allah') — both are correct, differing only in perspective.
The Imam takes the forms (suwarat) but the Mubda' al-Awwal does not take them; the governing decisions are made by the 'Aql al-Awwal even though the forms gather at the Mubda' al-Awwal.
When the Imam hands the gathered collection of forms (the imamat) to his farzand, the farzand — previously an Imam in potential made of riya' — goes from potential to actual.

Upon the Imam's passing the Bab al-Abwab also passes away and becomes the heart (qalb) of the Imam's farzand; this is illustrated by the death of Mawlana Abu Talib (the Imam) followed three days later by Khadija (his hujjat) in the Prophet's Year of Grief.
Mawlatuna Khadija is the Bab al-Abwab of Bibi Fatimah al-Zahra.

When the spheres cast their rays toward the earth, something of their nature returned to their essences and shells (asdaf) formed upon the non-visible spheres, rendering the stars visible but introducing negativity (nahusat) — so Zuhal, pure in essence, acquired inauspiciousness through its sadaf.

The stars in their original state were notional (wahmiyya) and invisible like the spheres; the Mudabbir made the asdaf by His wisdom so they would be perceptible and illuminate the dark physical world.

At the 'Ashir's call the fallen disobeyed saying 'la nasma'u wa la nuti'', accepting only the Mabda' Ta'ala and claiming equality (sawa'an bi-sawa'), thereby acknowledging only the first perfection while denying the second perfection attained by the intellects and the Mubda' al-Awwal.
Isbagh al-wudu' is performing ablution thoroughly three times; there is no established virtue (la fadila lahu) in doing it beyond the third, though one praying alone is not forbidden from more.
One leading prayer must not prolong tasbihat or recite long surahs, as weak or weary followers cannot bear it.
Density (kathafa) brings a being down while subtlety (latafa) raises it; spiritual progress is attained through subtlety, and the hayula fell from the realm of purity due to density.

The 'Ashir arranged the physical world by rank of purity: the seven spheres and planets from the purest (the repentant nadimin), the four mothers (fire, air, water, earth) from the middling (the doubters and bewildered), and the sakhra (core of the earth) from the densest (the insistent and arrogant).

The falak al-muhit, encompassing the entire realm, is called the gate of the spiritual world ('alam al-quds); beyond it lies first the world of life ('alam al-hayat), not directly the spiritual world.

Of those who repented with the 'Ashir's repentance, the group 'Ta'ibu bi-Tawbatihi' ascended as intellects with his group, while another group ('Labbu Nida'ahu', who answered his call) had a separate world of life created for them, containing the tamur (repository) and the spiritual Ka'ba connected to the physical Ka'ba.

The 'alam al-niyyat (world of intention) is the upper realm of our intentions at origination; after origination we remained passive, not joining the intellects who affirmed God's oneness, until we fell into the 'Ashir's illusory equality, and there our world of intention was established by our differing consciences.
The tamur, above the falak al-muhit in the world of life, holds the original essences of the mohtajibin (the veiled ones of the Imams) who did not enter the spiritual world.
The Prophet's mi'raj (ascension) reached only the falak al-muhit and then returned, because beyond it one cannot return without becoming an intellect.

The twelve constellations of the falak al-buruj are: Hamal (Aries), al-Thawr (Taurus), al-Jawza' (Gemini), al-Sartan (Cancer), al-Asad (Leo), al-Sunbula (Virgo), al-Mizan (Libra), al-'Aqrab (Scorpio), al-Qaws (Sagittarius), al-Jady (Capricorn), al-Dalw (Aquarius), and al-Hut (Pisces).

The seven planetary spheres in order are Zuhal (Saturn), Mushtari (Jupiter), Mirrikh (Mars), Shams (Sun), Zuhra (Venus), 'Utarid (Mercury), and Qamar (Moon); from their revolutions arose the spheres of ether and air (kurra-e-asir, kurra-e-nasim) and the four mothers.

The governing being assigned the planets to administer the physical world in sequence under Zuhal's overall governance (Mushtari, Mirrikh, Shams, Zuhra, 'Utarid as helpers), and in the seventh thousand-year period the first human came into being under Qamar's partnership.
The spheres revolve around the earth (with the Ka'ba as center point), not around the sun; modern science has changed its position on this three times.

The Mudabbir Ta'ala made the opposites (azdad) of the celestial bodies by His wisdom to illuminate the dark physical world, and the senses perceiving them confirms the power of the Planner and the soundness of the celestial world.
When the falak al-muhit moved, the atmosphere below the moon's sphere reached extreme heat and dryness — the nature of fire — and was named asir (ether), the first of the four mothers.

Every sphere has its own kawkab except the falak al-muhit and the falak al-buruj; the falak al-muhit is invisible (ghair-mar'i) and its single 24-hour total motion, called the divine motion, drives all the spheres and planets below it.

After death a person is divided into three: the surat-e-sharif goes instantly to its hadd-e-'ali on earth; the middle part (riyat), released after three days, goes to the spheres (mainly the moon's, also Jupiter and the Sun) to be refined; and the body's purification proceeds to the falak al-buruj over 360 years.
The body's purification journey through the zodiac takes 720 years ascending and descending plus 280 years, returning after 1000 years minus its namiya, hissiya, and natiqa faculties.
In one kaur (cycle) a believer's fuzlah repeats 360 times, and Sayyidna 'Ali wrote that a believer's body contains 360 nufus, each of which progresses each cycle by becoming a nafs.

If a believer's hadd-e-'ali has passed away with a good end, his form merges (muwazajat) with it; if the hadd-e-'ali is still alive, his form remains in the vicinity (jiwar) — guarding against loss should the hadd-e-'ali go astray.
If a hadd-e-'ali goes astray, the ascending one's form is removed and he is given another hadd-e-'ali.

When one who served the da'wat goes astray, his luminous form (surat-e-nayyirah) earned by his good deeds is separated from his bad form — as Da'ud ibn Qutb's noble form passed to Sayyidna Muhammad ibn Fu'ad, and Abu Bakr's luminous form (from his service to the Prophet) passed to his son Muhammad bin Abi Bakr.
One's hadd-e-'ali must be from the current Imam's hudud, never from the ranks of a previous Imam whose cycle (haikal) is over.

Promotion cannot be held back; a lower one (adna) cannot restrain his higher one, and if a hadd-e-'ali is promoted into the gathering assembly the lower one is simply assigned a replacement hadd-e-'ali.
In the daur-e-kashf returns occur every thousand years, but the people of the daur-e-qa'im (the final era, like us) return first and are not bound by the thousand-year rule.
A believer has only one hadd-e-'ali, but a hadd-e-'ali may have a whole congregation (majma') of believers.
The Prophet said that when a believer prays, two rows pray behind him — his unseen (ghair-mar'i) congregation of his hadd-e-'ali.
When a questioner asks a question he is often a medium through whom a form from his congregation, or his hadd-e-'ali, asks for its own satisfaction of knowledge.

The Quran's 'Innal-hasanati yudhhibnas-sayyi'at' means the believer's hasanat — his lower ranks (hudud-e-daniya), still engaged in tasbih and pursuit of knowledge — eliminate his evil deeds, namely the doubts and misgivings (shukuk wa shubhat) in his hadd-e-'ali.
Doubt is necessary for a believer because the plant of certainty (yaqin) always grows in the soil of doubt (shakk).

Ibrahim's request to see how the dead are revived ('li-yatma'inna qalbi') shows that certainty is above faith ('al-yaqinu fawqa al-iman'); his belief was iman, but the satisfaction of the heart he sought was yaqin.

A hadd-e-'ali is appointed only after one takes the 'ahd-e-sharif, which is the spiritual birth (wiladat-e-batini) as distinct from the physical birth (wiladat-e-zahiri); before it one cannot have a hadd-e-'ali or become a hadd (zimmah) for others, lacking the magnet to attract the iron.

The four mothers form in sequence by the spheres' diminishing motion: asir (ether, center of fire, invisible, its light concealed by divine wisdom), hawa (air, moderate), ma' (water, cold and flowing), and earth (extreme cold and dryness).
The Mudabbir willed the earth to be the place for the appearance of the mawalid (creations): mineral (ma'dan), vegetable (nabat), animal (hayawan), and human (the rational animal, hayawan-e-natiq).

The celestial rays struck the hard rock (sakhra), recoiled from its hardness, returned reflected and heated the earth's surface and air, producing nasim (the breeze, center of water) and zamharir (intense cold, the highest part of the nasim sphere).

The sun's opposite (sadaf/azdad), like all the celestial bodies', was formed from the rock mixture; the kawakib are noble in essence (made of the highest parts of the nadimin) but their azdad acquired inauspiciousness from the rock, which is the basis of planetary effects on people.
The markaz al-ma' (center of water) is not water itself; if one travels there, water is not present — it is only the center from which water is balanced.
The Quran's 'Wa-llahu anbatakum min al-ardi nabata' establishes two kinds of human creation: from the earth (more excellent and higher) and from spiritual parents (lower).

Resurrection is true ('innal-ba'tha haqqun') and is of two kinds: the believer's resurrection (raised in faith after dying in faith) and the Prophet's resurrection at the praised station (maqam mahmud), appearing from Quds, into which Salman al-Farsi entered first and then the Prophet.
A qutb is born at the beginning of every cycle; the qutb of this cycle was born in Sarandib, and the qutb of the very first cycle of the du'at was born in the Ka'ba — the place where 'Ali was born.
The Quran's 'wa anzalna al-hadid fihi ba'sun shadid' states iron was sent down from the sky, and reciting this verse on Tuesday has great virtue.

The two nodes (head and tail, ra's wa dhanab) lie beyond the moon's sphere, the tail more severe than the head; the evil concepts (tasawwur-e-qabih) of the opposites of the du'at, prophets, and nuqata' went to the head, and those of the Imams, hujjats, and awsiya went to the tail.
The Mudabbir ('Ashir al-Mudabbir) delegated the administration of the world to Zuhal (Saturn) by his own substance, and Zuhal administers for a thousand years.

From the intermingled natures arose vapors, dense clouds, and continuous non-beneficial rains (matar al-su', the evil rain mentioned in the Quran), which carry impurities down, whereas good rains bring down the purified luminous essences (fudulat-e-nayyirah) from the falak al-buruj.

The essence's purification journey runs from the first degree of the first zodiac to the last and back, 720 years total; the book being read (Sayyidna Mu'ayyad al-Shirazi's) supplies the Tahajjud du'a 'la tuksiranna ya Rabbi fi hadha al-safarana' (do not prolong our journey).

Spiritual progress moves from the physical world to the psychic world: the body becomes a nafs (namiya, hissiya, natiqa), reaches the station of the sura, then the station of the 'aql (intellect) on some distant day (yawman ma); once the form enters the Imam's haykal it is like a fixed deposit that progresses with the Imam.
The mizaj-e-muntazij of essences is ascending through vapors (bukharat) and descending through rainwater after purification.

Even unbelievers, infidels, and hypocrites return after 1000 years; after purification they reach the station of affirmations (ta'yidat) with a thousand-year lifespan, becoming in actuality the angels they were in potentiality.
Per Sayyidna 'Ali, of five times one is when prayers are accepted, namely 'inda nuzul al-ghayth (at the time of rainfall), because at that time the purified essences are descending and ascending.

When the people asked the Messenger to pray for rain and then for it to stop, he recited 'khuliqa al-insanu min 'ajal' (man was created of haste); a parallel rain miracle occurred in the time of Sayyidna Ghulam Husain at Gandipet, traced back through Sayyidna 'Ali bin Qutbuddin (author of Bahrat al-'Adillah) and Sayyidna Isma'il bin Hibatullah.

At his death Sayyidna Mu'ayyad al-Shirazi wept, saying 'mata yalhaku al-baytu ila rabbihi' (when will the house join its Lord) — the body (house) longing to join its noble form (Lord) — before his four student-du'at including Lamak bin Malik.

The principle 'al-mu'minu yanzuru bi-nurillah' (the believer sees with the light of God) was invoked by Sayyidna Ja'far regarding the 12-year-old Sayyidna Hasan Khan, foreseeing 'yakunu lahu sha'nun min sha'n' (he will have a great station); Hasan Khan later wrote 70 books in haqa'iq.

In Zuhal's first thousand years the earth became a surging sea ('Wa sarat al-ardu bahran muwwajan') and fermented essences (khama'ir) resembling Saturn's nature — iron, stone, copper, and the Sudanese, farmers (zarra'a), the wretched (ahl al-shaqa), and the harsh — were formed.

Mushtari (Jupiter) is the Sa'd-e-Akbar; Jupiter and Venus are the two auspicious planets (sa'dayn), and 'al-Mushtari bayna al-nahsayn' (Jupiter between the two inauspicious) is illustrated by the Prophet's grave lying between Abu Bakr and 'Umar.

The 14-rak'at prayer at the Prophet's Mosque is offered at the pillars (ras, maqam al-Tawbah, Hannanah, 'Ali, etc.), of which the eight rak'at at the pillars are most meritorious, alluding to the bearers of the Throne; the maqam al-Tawbah is the spot the Prophet said people would draw lots for if they knew its virtue.

The successive thousand-year planetary governances each fermented essences of matching nature: Mushtari (pious religious people, vegetation, crawling creatures), Mirrikh (commanders, soldiers, minerals), Shams (kings, ruby, gold), Zuhra (Arabs, women, singers, fruits, birds), and 'Utarid (scribes, ministers, accountants), preparing for the human's appearance in the seventh millennium.

The human person appeared in the seventh thousand years 'nabatan min al-ardi' (as a plant from the earth), per 'wa-Allahu anbatakum min al-ardi nabata'; dinosaurs and similar claims of science have no mention in this tradition and are fiction.

A hadd is a fixed limit or measurement, per the Quran's 'la ta'tadu hudud Allah... man yata'adda hudud Allahi faqad zalama nafsahu' (do not transgress Allah's limits; whoever does has wronged himself).

When a believer dies his namiya, hissiya, and natiqa souls instantly unite into the surah sharifah, which goes to its hadd-e-'ali — one superior to it in rank by only a nineteen-to-twenty difference, not a da'i or hujjat of the time.

The Tahiyyat al-Masjid's mamsulat (referents) include one's hadd-e-'ali and its hadd-e-'ali; as a gift to the mosque it requires reciting the descending surahs (Falaq then Nas), a practice otherwise reserved for obligatory prayers and the sunnah of fajr, giving it special status.
A living hadd-e-'ali does not stop the lower one's wrong deeds, but a knowledge-loving hadd-dani can incite his hadd-e-'ali toward the world of knowledge if the latter is disinclined to it.

The 'ahd-e-sharif is the greatest act of worship, surpassing obligatory prayers, Hajj, Zakat, and fasting; without it the surah sharif is never formed and no hadd-e-'ali can be appointed, so it is renewed yearly on Yawm al-Ghadir per 'wa-dhakkir fa-inna al-dhikra tanfa'u al-mu'minin'.

Through the 'ahd-e-sharif one receives a nuqta-e-nur (point of light) from one's own hadd in the spiritual world, from its inabat and tawbah, per the Quran's 'la tansa nasibaka min al-dunya' — meaning do not die without the 'ahd-e-sharif.

A minimal 'ahd-e-sharif can be completed in one's last moments by taking the name of the Imam of the time and sending blessings upon him; even loving and obeying the infallible Imam of the time (khalifat Allah fi al-ard) without a formal covenant is tremendously beneficial.

Children who die young (ahl-e-istighar) do not have a surah formed, but have a majma'-e-sighar that progresses; this assembly was first given to Bibi Fatimah al-Zahra then to Mawlana Baqir, and the children of the A'imma who die young form the majma'-e-mufritin, also under Bibi Fatimah's care.

The believer's journey after death proceeds from higher hudud to the Bab al-Abwab; when the haykal gathered there is complete, the Imam acquires it and hands it to his farzand, who thereby goes from Imam in potential to Imam in actuality.

The Imam hands the gathered majma' to his farzand in four days or four years; rarely Mawlana 'Abd al-Muttalib received the majma' before birth, so his mother said 'wulidtu shaybah' (I gave birth to an old man) because his hair was white.
The spiritual majma' of nasut and lahut runs completely parallel (mumathil) to the nasut: a rank attained in nasut corresponds exactly to the form's place in lahut, never higher or lower.

Animals that die their own death in the 6000 years died a halal death, like the pigeons of the Ka'ba and Madinah, which cannot be hunted yet die halal because they are formed from the fudlat of the mukasirin.

A mukasir is the da'wat teacher who breaks (kasr) his students' false beliefs and establishes correct belief through his hujjat; he carries the entire load of the da'wat from the Imam down to the lowest rank, like the feet bearing the body's weight.

As reward for their lifelong labor, jewels (jawahir), rubies (yawaqit), and salt form from the fudlat and bones of the mukasirin; the Prophet said 'al-milh qabl al-ta'am wa ba'd al-ta'am yaqta'u sab'ina da'an, awwaluha al-junun wa al-juzam' (salt before and after food wards off seventy diseases, the least being madness and leprosy).

The Quran's 'fas'alu ahl al-dhikr in kuntum la ta'lamun', per Imam Husayn, means the Ahl al-Bayt are the ahl al-dhikr; God divided the world into ahl al-dhikr and la ta'lamun, obliging the latter to ask, but not obliging the Ahl al-Bayt to answer.

In the seventh millennium the higher governor moved the sphere and vapors ascended from the dregs of minerals, plants, and animals, became clouds (ghuyum), and poured down as a pure rain ('amtaran safiyatan') that made shallow furrows (khudad) in the earth.

A second, nobler vapor rose from the furrows and poured down as rain 'shabihatun bi-maniy al-rajul' (like a man's semen) into the furrows 'shabihatun bi-arham al-nisa'' (like women's wombs), mixed with the woman-like water, and took form through the stages of creation over nine months by the Mudabbir's arrangement and the celestial bodies' influence.

After nine months the first human opened his eyes, inhaled the nasim, rolled in and absorbed the remaining oily water through his pores, was nourished first from his navel then sucked his thumb (from which his Creator caused pure milk to flow), explaining infants' thumb-sucking habit.
The first human spent nine months plus one full year in the pit, then stood up the size of a four-year-old child due to the greatness of his parents, who are the heaven and the earth.

The Imam has four things: his nasut, his lahut, his nafs, and his surah; in the obligatory four-rak'at prayer the higher first two rak'at allude to the Imam's nafs and surah sharif, the latter two to his nasut and lahut.

The Imam's nasut is made from the riya' of the believers and the hudud of the da'wat, and his lahut from their surat; both are borrowed, only the Imam's nafs and surah being his own, which is why celestial bodies and poison can affect his borrowed body.

The Imam's nafs-e-hissiyah is so exalted it bears all the nawasit, lawahiq, lahut, and nasut of the entire era; Amir al-Mu'minin 'Ali ibn Abi Talib's nafs-e-hissiyah carried the hayakil of all the A'imma from Hunays to Abu al-Qayyim.

The Imam is infallible, so 'Ali uprooting the gate of Khaybar 'la bi-quwwatin jismaniyyatin bal bi-quwwatin ruhaniyyah/rabbaniyyah' was an allusion to the strength granted by his muhtajib (veiled one), not physical strength.
The Imam, being infallible, fulfills our qisasat; any difficulty falls upon the riya' and the believers, not upon him, his original essence remaining far removed.
'Ali's words at the blow ('fuztu bi-Rabb al-Ka'bah') related to the qisasat; 'Ali was the bearer of the surat of 10,000 years (plus 3,000 years of fatrat).

The present Amir holds the jami'iyyat of 400,000 surat (seven daur-e-kashf and six daur-e-satr) in his seventh manifestation; he is the khalifah of the Qayyim, the Qayyim the khalifah of the 'Ashir, and while the Amir is the 'ayn-e-awwalah the Qayyim is the 'ayn-e-akhirah.

In each pit (khudad) males were created first and females afterward from the remaining water; multiple pits were created at Sarandib and across the 12 islands, including evil pits from which enemies and adversaries arose.
There is a city in Sarandib named Nur Eliya, said to be the manifestation (tajalli) of Mawlana 'Ali.
